PART 4 — The Real Problem

Seeta didn't have a knowledge problem.
She didn't have a talent problem.
She didn't even have an opportunity problem.
She had a confidence problem!!!

And she wasn't alone.
We've all met people like Seeta.
Maybe you've worked with one.
Maybe you've managed one.
Maybe…
you are one!!!

The person who knows the answer.
But doesn't raise their hand.
The person with the story.
But doesn't tell it.
The person with potential.
But doesn't believe they belong in the room.

Part 5 tomorrow.
comment: Confidence gaps often get mistaken for capability gaps. In teams, the fix is not just encouragement—it’s creating environments where people can safely contribute before they feel completely ready.
